name: PTF09cnd field (Hubble)
blurb: The host galaxy of the superluminous supernova PTF09cnd, seen by Hubble.
label: ptf09cnd-hubble
story: The galaxy that once hosted PTF09cnd, one of the brightest kinds of stellar explosion, a superluminous supernova. Hubble came back to pin down where in its host the blast occurred, part of a hunt for the stars behind the most luminous supernovae, perhaps very massive stars poor in heavy elements.

claims.text: PTF09cnd is a superluminous supernova (SLSN-I) whose host was imaged by Hubble program GO-13025
The program surveyed host galaxies of the brightest supernovae
The program aimed to locate the supernovae within their hosts
A possible origin is very massive, low-metallicity stars
The program is titled for the most luminous supernovae
Superluminous supernovae are among the brightest supernovae
